rationale: Greek λύπη/λυπεῖν 'grief, sorrow' as Coptic verbalized form ⲣ̄- + λύπη. Used as the structuring verb of this kephalaion ('Four Powers of Those Who Grieve'). Standard Greek loanword for affective grief/sorrow.

proposed_english: the other death / the second death
rationale: ⲡⲕⲉ- 'the other' + ⲙⲟⲩ 'death.' Manichaean eschatological term for the second/eternal death contrasted with the first (= bodily) death. Cf. ⲡⲙⲟⲩ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'the two deaths' in accumulated vocabulary.

proposed_english: to exceed / to surpass (or to diminish — uncertain)
rationale: Recurring verb on this page (lines 3, 12). In line 3 'ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲭⲃⲉ ⲁⲛⲉⲓ̈' = 'they did not X these.' Antithesis with ⲡϩⲟⲩⲟ ⲁⲛⲉⲓ 'the surplus/excess of these' in line 4 suggests 'exceed/surpass.' But could also mean 'diminish/be fewer than.' Direction uncertain.
Lyc. nominalizing prefix ⲧⲟⲓⲛ- (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ, ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲛⲟⲩϩⲙⲉ in vocabulary) on stem ⲱⲱ 'conceive.' Action-noun: 'the conceiving.'
Same nominalizing pattern: ⲧⲟⲓⲛ-ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'the bearing.' Paired with ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ̄ⲱ 'conception' as conception+birth dyad.
Standard Coptic ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'bear, beget' nominalized. Recurs through this page as the central topic-noun of the kephalaion on generations.
Lyc. variant of ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the First Man' (in accumulated vocabulary). The shortened ⲱⲁⲣ for ⲱⲁⲣⲡ is a recognized scribal contraction.

proposed_english: the Mother of the Living One
rationale: ⲙⲙⲟ = Lyc. for ⲙⲁⲁⲩ 'mother'; ⲡⲧⲱⲛϩ̄ = Lyc. for ⲡⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ̄ / ⲡⲱⲛϩ̄ 'the Living One.' Identical in reference to ⲧⲙⲁⲁⲩ ⲙⲡⲱⲛϩ̄ = Mater Viventium (Mother of Life). First of the Four Grieving Powers.
ⲡⲏⲱ tentatively qualitative of ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'incline, change.' With ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'of heart' = 'turned/inclined of heart' — characterization of the grieving powers whose hearts incline toward the suffering souls.
Reading uncertain. Possibilities: 'their husbands' (ⲛⲉⲩ-ϩⲁⲓ), 'their last/posterity' (ⲛⲉⲩ-ϩⲁⲏ), or part of compound 'their multitude' (ⲛⲉⲩ-ϩⲁ-ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ). Pending parallels.
